title: Group-like elements in a group algebra over a field are basis elements
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $M$ be an abelian group, written additively with identity $0$. Write $k[M]=\bigoplus_{m\in M}ke^m$ for the commutative $k$-algebra of finite formal sums, with $e^me^n=e^{m+n}$ and unit $e^0$. Equip it with the $k$-linear comultiplication $\Delta(e^m)=e^m\otimes e^m$ and counit $\varepsilon(e^m)=1$, where the tensor product has the algebra structure of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. For every $a\in k[M]$,
$$\bigl(\varepsilon(a)=1\ \text{and}\ \Delta(a)=a\otimes a\bigr)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists m\in M,\ a=e^m.$$
The conjunction on the left is the definition of being group-like.
